h1:
Buriram Cafes 2026
10 Spots in Town & Around Chang Arena
intro: Buriram isn't just stone temples and a football stadium. Over the past few years the town has seen a real wave of new cafes — small spots in town that are walkable to each other, places around Chang Arena you can stop at before or after a match, and leafy garden cafes that photograph well. The nice thing about cafes here is that they're nowhere near as crowded as the big tourist towns: easy seating, fair prices. We picked 10 places that are genuinely open and that reviewers keep mentioning — a mix for serious coffee drinkers, photo people, and anyone who wants to settle in for a while.

blocks.html: Before the ranking, here's the honest layout: Buriram's town-center cafes are very close together — many are just a few minutes' drive apart. The places around Chang Arena sit only about 4–5 km from town, so they're an easy stop on the way to a game. This list focuses on places with a real storefront, open for a while, with a steady stream of genuine reviews. We've split it into three groups — serious coffee shops in town · photo-friendly cafes · and spots around Chang Arena. All prices are rough ranges, so check the cafe's page again before you go, since hours and menus change often.

blocks.text: For serious coffee — in Buriram town

blocks.html: If you've come to Buriram and want a properly good cup, the town center has several places that take their beans and brewing seriously. Many offer both espresso drinks and pour-overs, so you can order to your own spec.

items.name: unbox.project cafe
items.blurb: A two-floor minimalist cafe in town, and one of the spots serious coffee people talk about most. There's a rotating selection of beans, including Ethiopian, plus cakes and baked goods made in-house and nicely presented. Good if you want serious coffee in a relaxed, low-key setting.

items.name: Earth Coffee & Community
items.blurb: A white, minimalist place with an indoor garden zone for relaxed seating. The draw is the range of drinks — coffee, hojicha, and cocoa — and there are plenty of photo corners. Locals use it as a meeting spot and a place to get work done; the space feels open and easy.

items.name: Jamsai Brewing Space
items.blurb: A warm, cozy cafe in the Nong Paep area of town. There's a big drinks list — matcha, coffee, milk-based menus — and they sell beans too. What sets it apart is the little activities, like DIY keychains and a flower corner, so it suits both coffee people and anyone who wants something fun to do.

items.name: TREEORTHREE.coffee
items.blurb: A glamping-styled cafe in town — it feels like sitting in a tent in the forest, but with air conditioning. The most-ordered items are the soft cheesecake, Thai tea, and coconut pudding. Prices are friendly, and it's a good pick if you want something different from the usual minimalist spots.

blocks.title: Tip for coffee people
blocks.html: Buriram's town cafes are very close together — just a few minutes' drive apart. If you want to try several in one day, start with the early openers like unbox or Earth, then move on to the later ones. Some of the smaller places have limited seating and get busy on Saturday and Sunday afternoons, so going before noon is more comfortable.

blocks.text: For photos — good vibes and pretty corners

blocks.html: If your goal is a good shot for the feed and a comfortable place to sit, Buriram has several cafes that put real thought into their photo corners — from Japanese-style spots to places with gardens and a small artificial waterfall.

items.name: Bansai Cafe
items.blurb: A clean, simple minimalist cafe in town with the full lineup — coffee, bubble tea, and bakery. The clean styling makes it easy to photograph, and it's a nice spot to relax in the afternoon. It opens early at 7am; weekdays close in the evening, while weekends run later.

items.name: Cher Cafe
items.blurb: A cafe with a natural garden zone — there's the sound of an artificial waterfall and fish swimming in a pond. It's shaded, cool, and a nice break if you want to swap the white minimalist look for some greenery. The photo corners lean toward garden and water.
items.meta: Buriram town center · check the page for hours before you go

items.name: La Paz Cafe
items.blurb: A white-brown-cream cafe in a Japanese minimalist style, with good natural light that makes for nice photos. It's known for soft cakes and on-trend drinks, at prices that aren't expensive — good if you like clean, simple corners.

blocks.text: Around Chang Arena — stop before or after the match

blocks.html: Chang Arena sits just outside town, about 4–5 km to the east, near Khao Kradong. On match days the area around the stadium gets packed. If you want a spot to rest before heading in, or somewhere to wait out the traffic after the final whistle, the cafes in this zone work better than diving back into town.

items.name: SUNBAKED
items.blurb: A newer cafe in a white minimalist design, about 1.5 km from the lane beside Chang Arena — an easy stop before heading into the stadium. The popular orders are the croffle, tiramisu, and drinks like Matcha Yuzu Soda. There's both indoor and outdoor seating.

items.name: Khao Kradong-area cafe
items.blurb: Along the foot of Khao Kradong on the way to the stadium, there's a chic minimalist cafe with both indoor and outdoor zones, serving americano and a range of desserts. The plus is its location near both Khao Kradong temple and the stadium, so you can sightsee and sip coffee in one loop.
items.meta: Foot of Khao Kradong, on the way to the stadium · roughly 8:00–18:00

items.name: L TWIN Cafe
items.blurb: A small, quiet cafe by a canal, in town on the route heading toward Chang Arena. It's a good place to duck away from the match-day chaos for a bit. Coffee starts around ฿80. We close out the list with a small, quiet spot where seating is comfortable and you won't have to fight for a table.
items.meta: In town, on the route to the stadium · Sat–Sun 9:00–18:00

blocks.title: On match days at Chang Arena
blocks.html: On days when Buriram United plays at home, traffic around the stadium gets heavy in the 1–2 hours before kickoff. If you're stopping for a cafe, finish up at the stadium-zone spots before the crowds pour in, then walk or drive the rest of the way to the ground. After the final whistle the cafes near the stadium fill up fast — if you're not in a hurry, it's more comfortable to wait for the traffic to thin before you head out.

blocks.text: Why Buriram cafes are worth a stop

blocks.html: What sets Buriram cafes apart from the big tourist towns is that they're still not as packed, the seating is comfortable, and the prices aren't steep. Many are run by younger locals who came back to open up in their hometown, so they put real care into both the coffee and the atmosphere. Getting around is easy too — the town is small, so driving from one side to the other doesn't take long.

items: Friendly prices — most coffees run around ฿55–130 a cup, cheaper than cafes in the big tourist towns.
Sightsee and sip in one loop — the cafes around Khao Kradong and the stadium are near the sights, so they fit neatly into the route.
Town cafes are walkable to each other — the town is small, and many cafes are just a few minutes' drive apart, making a cafe-hopping trip easy to plan.

blocks.text: How to pick a cafe to match your trip

items.name: Here for a match at Chang Arena
items.blurb: Go for the stadium-zone spots — SUNBAKED, the Khao Kradong cafe, or L TWIN, which sits on the route to the ground. Stop in before kickoff or wait out the traffic after the game.

items.name: Want genuinely good coffee
items.blurb: Head to the places that take their beans seriously — unbox.project, Earth Coffee, or Jamsai — which all offer both espresso and pour-over options.

items.name: Mainly here for photos and chilling
items.blurb: Pick the spots with well-planned corners — Bansai, La Paz, or Cher, which has a green garden zone — for nice photos and comfortable seating.

faq.q: Which Buriram cafes are near Chang Arena?
faq.a: The ones near or on the route to the stadium are SUNBAKED, about 1.5 km from the lane beside the ground; the cafe at the foot of Khao Kradong on the way to the stadium; and L TWIN Cafe, in town on the route heading to the ground. All are easy stops before or after a match.

faq.q: Are the cafes in Buriram town close together — can you visit several in one day?
faq.a: Buriram town is small, and many cafes are just a few minutes' drive apart, so a cafe-hopping trip is easy to plan. We'd suggest starting with the early openers like unbox.project or Earth Coffee, then moving on to the spots that open later in the afternoon.

faq.q: Roughly how much does coffee cost at Buriram cafes?
faq.a: Most run around ฿55–130 a cup, cheaper than cafes in the big tourist towns. Some, like Earth Coffee, start at around ฿60, while specialty or single-origin pour-overs can run a bit higher. Check the cafe's menu page before you go.

faq.q: Which Buriram cafe is good for long working sessions?
faq.a: Earth Coffee & Community is an open, white-toned place with a garden zone that locals often use for working. Jamsai Brewing Space also has a warm vibe that suits settling in for a while. Avoid Saturday and Sunday afternoons when it gets busy, and check there are enough outlets before you set up camp.

faq.q: Do you need your own car to do the Buriram cafes?
faq.a: In town the cafes are close together and you can reach them by taxi or motorbike taxi. But for the spots around Chang Arena and the Khao Kradong area, which sit about 4–5 km outside town, having your own car or a rental is much more convenient.
